rule: decision 47: a mapping the blind verifier did not confirm is held — never shown, never a diagnosis, never S5 evidence — until a human keeps or drops it

items.stem: Represent graphically the function $\ell(x) = -2x$. Drag the two points so the line is the graph.
items.construction: Equation mode, m=-2, b=0: drag the handles to (0,0) and (1,-2) (or (-1,2) and (1,-2)). The line y=-2x passes through them; any two points on it are accepted. Neither is at (-3,-2) or (1,1) restrictions, and points mode limits don't apply.
items.predicate_meaning: Slope taken as run over rise instead of rise over run
items.hint: Use your table: for each step of 1 to the right, how many units does the line move up or down?
items.why: Fires with m=-1/2 (e.g. (0,0),(2,-1)), but the hint says 'Use your table' and this question has no table, so the student has nothing to refer to.

items.stem: Represent graphically the function $\ell(x) = -2x$. Drag the two points so the line is the graph.
items.construction: Equation mode, m=-2, b=0: drag the handles to (0,0) and (1,-2) (or (-1,2) and (1,-2)). The line y=-2x passes through them; any two points on it are accepted. Neither is at (-3,-2) or (1,1) restrictions, and points mode limits don't apply.
items.predicate_meaning: A vertical line, which has no slope and cannot be written y = mx + c
items.hint: Each x has exactly one image, so the graph cannot be vertical. Use the table of pairs.
items.why: Can fire (two points with the same x), and the reasoning about one image per x is right, but it points to 'the table of pairs', which this question doesn't provide.

items.stem: Represent graphically the function $f(x) = 5$. Drag the two points so the line is the graph.
items.construction: Equation mode with m=0, b=5: place the two handles at (-2,5) and (2,5), giving the horizontal line y=5. Both are lattice points in range and avoid the opening handle spots (-3,-2) and (1,1). Any two points with y=5 and different x also work.
items.predicate_meaning: A vertical line, which has no slope and cannot be written y = mx + c
items.hint: Every x has the same image, so the points have different x but the same y. Does that give a vertical line?
items.why: It can fire when both points share an x. But the hint says every x has the same image and that the points need different x and the same y. That is the construction of the answer, a horizontal line, so it gives the answer away.

items.stem: Represent graphically the function $f(x) = 5$. Drag the two points so the line is the graph.
items.construction: Equation mode with m=0, b=5: place the two handles at (-2,5) and (2,5), giving the horizontal line y=5. Both are lattice points in range and avoid the opening handle spots (-3,-2) and (1,1). Any two points with y=5 and different x also work.
items.predicate_meaning: Right gradient, wrong sign — the line leans the other way
items.hint: Compare the images in your table: do they change as x changes?
items.why: The correct slope is 0, so there is no sign to flip. A line with slope -0 is the correct slope and cannot fire this predicate. The hint's table-of-images advice does not match any student error here.

items.stem: Represent graphically the function $f(x) = -4$. Drag the two points so the line is the graph.
items.construction: Equation mode, y = 0x - 4. Drag the two handles to (-2,-4) and (2,-4); the line through them is horizontal at y = -4. m=0 is a whole number and b=-4 is within -5..5.
items.predicate_meaning: A vertical line, which has no slope and cannot be written y = mx + c
items.hint: Every x has the same image, so the points have different x but the same y. Does that give a vertical line?
items.why: A student who confuses f(x) = -4 with x = -4 and places both points at x = -4 gets a vertical line, so the predicate can fire. The hint says the points need different x but the same y. That is the construction of the answer, so it gives the step away. It also asks 'does that give a vertical line?' while describing a horizontal one, which is muddled.

items.stem: Represent graphically the function $f(x) = 0$. Drag the two points so the line is the graph.
items.construction: Equation mode with m=0, b=0: drag the two handles to lattice points (0,0) and (2,0) (any two points on the x-axis, e.g. (-3,0),(4,0)). The line y=0 is drawn. m=0 is a whole number and b=0 is within -5..5, so it satisfies every limit.
items.predicate_meaning: A vertical line, which has no slope and cannot be written y = mx + c
items.hint: Every x has the same image, so the points have different x but the same y. Does that give a vertical line?
items.why: Fires with two points of equal x, e.g. (2,0) and (2,3). The hint says the points have different x but the same y, which describes a horizontal line, not a vertical one. It is mathematically wrong and would confuse a student who built a vertical line. It also says every x has the same image, which is the actual answer's property.
